cases.sentence: Он сидел в расстегнутом над белым жилетом сюртуке, облокотившись обеими руками на стол, и, ожидая заказанного бифстека, смотрел в книгу ___, лежавшую на тарелке.
cases.explain: «французского романа» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: On the day of the races at Krasnoe Selo, Vronsky had come earlier than usual to eat beefsteak in the common messroom of the regiment. He had no need to be strict with himself, as he had very quickly been brought down to the required light weight; but still he had to avoid gaining flesh, and so he eschewed farinaceous and sweet dishes. He sat with his coat unbuttoned over a white waistcoat, resting both elbows on the table, and while waiting for the steak he had ordered he looked at a French novel that lay open on his plate. He was only looking at the book to avoid conversation with the officers coming in and out; he was thinking.

cases.sentence: Он виделся с ней в ___ на даче у кузины Бетси.
cases.explain: «последний раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He was thinking of Anna’s promise to see him that day after the races. But he had not seen her for three days, and as her husband had just returned from abroad, he did not know whether she would be able to meet him today or not, and he did not know how to find out. He had had his last interview with her at his cousin Betsy’s summer villa. He visited the Karenins’ summer villa as rarely as possible. Now he wanted to go there, and he pondered the question how to do it.

cases.sentence: – Пошли ко мне на дом, чтобы закладывали поскорей коляску тройкой, – сказал он слуге, подававшему ему бифстек на серебряном ___, и, придвинув блюдо, стал есть.
cases.explain: «горячем блюде» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Send to my house, and tell them to have out the carriage and three horses as quick as they can,” he said to the servant, who handed him the steak on a hot silver dish, and moving the dish up he began eating.

cases.sentence: Из входной двери появились два офицера: – один молоденький, с слабым, тонким лицом, недавно поступивший из ___ в их полк; другой пухлый, старый офицер с браслетом на руке и заплывшими маленькими глазами.
cases.explain: «Пажеского корпуса» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: From the billiard room next door came the sound of balls knocking, of talk and laughter. Two officers appeared at the entrance-door: one, a young fellow, with a feeble, delicate face, who had lately joined the regiment from the Corps of Pages; the other, a plump, elderly officer, with a bracelet on his wrist, and little eyes, lost in fat.

cases.sentence: – Что? подкрепляешься на работу? – сказал ___, садясь подле него.
cases.explain: «пухлый офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What? Fortifying yourself for your work?” said the plump officer, sitting down beside him.

cases.sentence: – А не боишься потолстеть? – сказал тот, поворачивая стул для ___.
cases.explain: «молоденького офицера» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “So you’re not afraid of getting fat?” said the latter, turning a chair round for the young officer.

cases.sentence: – Что? – сердито сказал Вронский, делая гримасу отвращения и показывая свои ___.
cases.explain: «сплошные зубы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “What?” said Vronsky angrily, making a wry face of disgust, and showing his even teeth.

cases.sentence: ___ взял карту вин и обратился к молоденькому офицеру.
cases.explain: «Пухлый офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The plump officer took up the list of wines and turned to the young officer.

cases.sentence: – Пожалуй, рейнвейну, – сказал ___, робко косясь на Вронского и стараясь поймать пальцами чуть отросшие усики.
cases.explain: «молодой офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Rhine wine, please,” said the young officer, stealing a timid glance at Vronsky, and trying to pull his scarcely visible mustache. Seeing that Vronsky did not turn round, the young officer got up.

cases.sentence: И он сел подле Вронского, согнув ___ свои слишком длинные по высоте стульев стегна и голени в узких рейтузах. – Что ж ты вчера не заехал в красненский театр?
cases.explain: «острыми углами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “There go the inseparables,” Yashvin dropped, glancing sarcastically at the two officers who were at that instant leaving the room. And he bent his long legs, swathed in tight riding breeches, and sat down in the chair, too low for him, so that his knees were cramped up in a sharp angle. “Why didn’t you turn up at the Red Theater yesterday? Numerova wasn’t at all bad. Where were you?”
